title: ResourceLoader native singleton function exist() doesn't work correctly when used with type_hint argument.
body:
### Tested versions

-Reproductible in 4.4.1.stable: 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5001f43-85c1-4322-b520-384f11425c3a) , 

4.4.0.stable THIS IS ORIGINAL PROJECT WHERE FIND ERROR, NOT MINIMAL REPRODUCTIBLE: 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81fe87f3-2552-4524-9346-8c09a5a606ee), 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c27f4e8c-073d-44b9-9463-601c8ba03671),

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8654c5e0-b638-4636-89c9-7f86573f5177)

3.5.3.stable:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac81689e-eeea-4b3e-be0a-de5d1e60cf09)

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sonoma (14.7.3) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 (Apple8) - Apple M2 (8 threads)

### Issue description

**When you use ResourceLoader.exist("path_to_check", "type_to_check"):

- sometimes it works (returns true if the path refers to a file of the type_hint specified and false if it refers to another kind of file) 
- but sometimes it doesn't (always returns true).** 



In the project i originally encounter the problem i wanted to check if the resource was a PackedScene and if it wasn't throw an error. But when i was testing i pass a script (GDScript type) and it also allow (the function returns true) so it causes problems. 

So I try with other resources to see what happens and some worked some didn't. 

Then when i was going to post the **ISSUE**, i created a new project for using as a minimal reproducible project and i do it in many versions of godot (4.4.1, 4.4.0 this was the original, 4.2, 4.0, and 3.5).

And for my surprise other types were the ones causing problems:

- In the original .gd, .png and .otf were causing problems; 
- and in the minimal reproducible project in 4.4, as in 4.4.1, only .png and .otf were causing problems; 
- in 4.2 again .gd was causing problem and also .png as in 4.0; 
- but in 3.5 .gd wasnt causing problems but png does. 



**There is no clear conclution as not even in the same version of Godot (as in my original project and in my minimal reproductible project in 4.4.0) the erratically behavior is the same. But it seems the problem is ocurring maily in graphics resourses and scripts.**  

### Steps to reproduce

The only thing you have to do is run the scene or project and see the output. if you want you can use other resources also. 

I leave you a minimal reproduction project here. 

It is just a project with a scene called main.tscn with just a node called Main that have a script called main.gd attached. And a folder with some resources to test. A png file, a scene, a script and an .otf file(font file) and a video .ogv. 

In the main.gd, in the _ready() function creates an array with the paths to the resources and then it iterates over that array, printing the result of calling the ResoursceLoader.exist() function over those paths. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[testproject4.1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19740461/testproject4.1.zip)
